articles.title: Shohei Ohtani bats sixth in Dodgers' NLCS Game 3 lineup, his lowest start since 2020
articles.summary: Ohtani is 1-for-7 through two games of the NLCS.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts promised Tuesday that Shohei Ohtani would remain in the team's lineup for Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday against the Milwaukee Brewers.

The lineup was released Wednesday afternoon, and it showed Ohtani batting sixth — the lowest he has ever appeared in the batting order during his time with the Dodgers.

Ohtani will follow Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Andy Pages. He'll bat ahead of Will Smith, Miguel Rojas and Tommy Edman.

Roberts said after his team's loss in Game 2 that they would discuss what is best for Ohtani, as the slugger is just 1-for-7 at the plate in the series while fighting through knee and biceps injuries. The Milwaukee Brewers lead the series 2-0.

"Yeah, I mean, obviously, it hasn't been good. He doesn't feel great. I think for me, it's having a conversation with him tomorrow, kind of try to figure out what's best for him, what's best for us. He certainly has earned that conversation and deserves it. "I'll have [that conversation] with him tomorrow."

"Yeah, I mean, obviously, it hasn't been good. He doesn't feel great. I think for me, it's having a conversation with him tomorrow, kind of try to figure out what's best for him, what's best for us. He certainly has earned that conversation and deserves it.

"I'll have [that conversation] with him tomorrow."

Ohtani reportedly said he was "very convicted" about improving and "adamant" he feels good enough to play, per MLB.com's Sonja Chen .

Following Roberts' announcement, the designated hitter spoke to the media through interpreter Will Ireton . He said, in part, "I take full responsibility. … The symptoms shouldn't be the reason why I can't hit."

Ohtani spoke about how his injuries have improved. "The symptoms have subdued a lot, especially when I was on the IL," he said. "As of now, the swing is a daily process of trying different things."

Ohtani's struggles have not been limited to this series. He's 3-for-20 with three walks and seven strikeouts in the postseason. He hasn't registered an extra-base hit, as all three of his hits have been singles. Over his six postseason games so far, he is slashing just .150/.261/.150.

The Dodgers slugger missed much of the final month of the regular season due to knee and biceps injuries. Since Aug. 14, he slashed .198/.305/.363 in his final 23 regular-season games.

Ohtani was added to the IL in September and didn't play from Sept. 9 to Sept. 23. When he was activated, he was still dealing with issues. He admitted ahead of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves that he would need to " manage " both injuries through the playoffs.

The Dodgers' designated hitter hit fourth in the series opener but then was dropped to fifth in the order for Game 2 — his lowest start in the batting order since 2020 with the L.A. Angels.

The NLCS is a best-of-seven series. Game 3 is Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Astros’ 4 best Joe Espada manager replacements
articles.summary: The Houston Astros are officially searching for a new manager after deciding not to renew Joe Espada’s contract following three seasons at the helm. Espada h...
articles.body:
The Houston Astros are officially searching for a new manager after deciding not to renew Joe Espada 's contract following three seasons at the helm. Espada helped Houston win two American League West titles, but the team's recent postseason struggles ultimately led the organization in a different direction. Now, the Astros must identify the right person to lead a roster that still has championship aspirations but needs to prove it can compete consistently in October.

Houston has several potential options, ranging from familiar faces within the organization to experienced managers and former players looking to make the jump into the dugout. It should be noted that Omar Lopez, the current Astros bench coach, has already been offered a different role to stay with the team . While he could get an interview for the job, it seems the organization wants a new face in the building.

Here are four candidates the Astros should consider (in no particular order) as they begin their search for Espada's replacement.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Ausmus offers Houston a combination of organizational familiarity and major league managerial experience. The former Astros catcher has deep ties to the franchise and previously interviewed for the team's managerial opening before Dusty Baker was hired.

Ausmus managed the Detroit Tigers from 2014 through 2017 and the Los Angeles Angels in 2019. Those experiences give him an understanding of the responsibilities and challenges that come with leading a major league clubhouse. He has since worked as the New York Yankees' bench coach, continuing to gain experience on a staff competing under significant expectations.

Houston would be taking a calculated risk by bringing Ausmus back into the organization in a leadership role, but his background makes him a candidate. His familiarity with the franchise could help him adapt quickly.

Linares would be another appealing option for an organization that values player development and familiarity with its personnel. He spent 21 seasons in Houston's organization, managing throughout the minor leagues before joining Tampa Bay's major league coaching staff.

During his time in Houston's farm system, Linares worked with several players who became central figures in the Astros' success, including José Altuve and Carlos Correa. He now serves as the Rays' bench coach, giving him additional experience working alongside a major league manager.

Linares has not managed at the major league level, which would make his hiring a significant step. However, his extensive experience developing talent and his familiarity with Houston's organizational structure could help him establish credibility with the clubhouse.

Albert Pujols , Dominican Republic Manager

Pujols would represent a much different direction for Houston, but his name deserves consideration. The Hall of Fame slugger has expressed interest in becoming a major league manager and has already gained experience leading teams after his playing career. He managed the Dominican Republic in the 2026 World Baseball Classic and previously interviewed for the San Diego Padres' managerial opening .

Pujols would bring immediate credibility to a clubhouse filled with accomplished veterans. His playing career gives him firsthand knowledge of the pressures elite athletes face, and his leadership could resonate with established stars.

The obvious concern is his lack of major league managerial experience. Managing a national team loaded with talent is different from navigating a 162-game season, managing a pitching staff and making adjustments over several months. Still, Houston could consider Pujols if it believes his leadership and baseball knowledge outweigh the risks.

Banister would give Houston an experienced option who already understands the American League West. He managed the Texas Rangers from 2015 through 2018, won two division titles and earned American League Manager of the Year honors in 2015.

His familiarity with the division could be valuable as Houston attempts to reclaim its place among the American League's top teams. Banister also has previous connections to the Astros, having interviewed for the organization's managerial position before the team hired A.J. Hinch.

Banister has since continued his coaching career, most recently serving as the Arizona Diamondbacks' bench coach. His combination of managerial experience, division knowledge, and familiarity with Houston makes him a candidate if the Astros prefer an established leader over a first-time manager.

Ultimately, Houston's next hire must do more than maintain the status quo. The Astros need someone who can manage a demanding clubhouse, maximize the roster's talent, and help the team translate regular-season success into postseason wins. Each of these five candidates offers a different path forward, but the organization must decide which leadership style gives it the best chance to return to championship contention.

articles.title: NLCS: Jackson Chourio sucks life out of Dodger Stadium with first-pitch home run off Blake Snell to spark Brewers' Game 3
articles.summary: Chourio's was the first of three home runs Snell surrendered to the Brewers as Milwaukee pushed the Dodgers to the brink.
articles.body:
Well, that was a buzzkill for Dodgers fans.

With the Brewers holding a 2-0 lead in the National League Championship Series, the Dodgers were hoping some home-cooking could right the ship with the series shifting to Los Angeles on Wednesday.

That's Brewers leadoff hitter Jackson Chourio hitting a leadoff home run against two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell on the first pitch of the game for a quick 1-0 Milwaukee lead. Snell left a fastball over the heart of the plate, and Chourio made him pay.

The fans who'd beaten Los Angeles traffic to show up for the 5 p.m. local start barely had time to get settled in their seats before the air was sucked out of Dodger Stadium.

The Dodgers rallied to take a 2-1 lead in the sixth inning, but the Brewers punched right back in the seventh with two more home runs off Snell.

Jake Bauers capped an 11-pitch at-bat with a two-run home to retake the lead for Milwaukee 3-2.

Two pitches later, Snell surrendered a solo shot to Garrett Mitchell that extended Milwaukee's lead to 4-2.

And that was enough for Milwaukee to stun the Los Angeles crowd with a 6-2 Game 3 win that featured three home runs off of Snell. The Brewers hold a 3-0 series lead, leaving the Dodgers in need of a historic effort to advance to a third consecutive World Series.

The only team to rally from a 3-0 deficit in MLB playoff history was the 2004 Boston Red Sox, who vanquished the rival New York Yankees en route to their first World Series title since 1918.

articles.title: How the Small-Market Brewers Put the Dodgers' $500M Dynasty on Life Support
articles.summary: Those who would weep for the Los Angeles Dodgers right now are in the minority. They can spend $500 million on a roster all they want, but money like that doesn't buy sympathy when it's on the verge of failure.
articles.body:
Those who would weep for the Los Angeles Dodgers right now are in the minority. They can spend $500 million on a roster all they want, but money like that doesn't buy sympathy when it's on the verge of failure.

This is a story of the National League Championship Series. Don't confuse it with the story. Despite costing a third as much as their opponent, the Milwaukee Brewers have been the better team, running up a 3-0 lead to put themselves on the verge of a sweep to the World Series.

The Brewers overwhelmed the Dodgers in the first two games, wearing out Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto and allowing only one extra-base hit to Dodgers hitters. In the seventh inning of Game 3, Milwaukee made Dave Roberts pay for his lack of faith in his bullpen, getting to Blake Snell for game-breaking back-to-back home runs as the lefty was approaching 100 pitches.

It's as if the Brewers truly deserve to be crowned as the National League's best team. Go figure, after they won an MLB-best 103 regular-season games.

And so, with apologies to J.R.R. Tolkien , the Dodgers' quest for a World Series three-peat stands upon the edge of a knife. They can and should blame themselves. The rest of us can and should credit the Brewers.

When criticizing the Dodgers, you must follow a certain ritual. It involves doing an awkward dance while acknowledging that they are, in fact, a well-run franchise.

It's impossible to separate their sheer quality from the sheer might of their resources. It's also impossible to ignore questions about how team owner Mark Walter accesses those resources. Yet president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman is ultimately the architect here, and he gets high marks for using free agency, trades and player development to keep the machine humming.

The Dodgers have won the NL West 11 times in 12 seasons under Friedman. They are typically in the top five of the NL in runs scored and runs allowed. They hit a lot of home runs. They strike a lot of guys out. It's clearly a winning formula.

However, this formula has its limits, as was evident even as the Dodgers basked in the afterglow of their second straight World Series championship last October.

An offense that was getting older and less productive clearly needed to get younger and more dynamic. Fixing the problem should have been more complicated than simply signing Kyle Tucker , and even his four-year, $240 million contract smacked more of hubris than good sense. A 29-year-old player is more middle-aged than young these days, and he had spent a good chunk of the last two seasons limited by injuries.

The poor season Tucker had this year was always a possibility, and its occurrence (97 OPS+) doomed the lineup to more pain from the sub-prime seasons of 36-year-old Freddie Freeman (118 OPS+) and 33-year-old Mookie Betts (113 OPS+).

Shohei Ohtani could have saved the Dodgers, and he did for a time as he cranked 30 home runs with a .949 OPS through August 18. At some point, though, the pain in his left knee and right arm became an open secret. The Dodgers just let him keep playing through it… and playing through it… and playing through it.

The bill for that has come due. The four-time MVP didn't feel healthy even after a two-week IL stint in September, and now he looks worse than he's letting on. Ohtani's beautiful swing has devolved into bad performance art. No wonder he's hit no homers and has one RBI since August 19.

It's Ohtani's track record, reputation and aura keeping him in the lineup, and at the expense of someone who is right there to give the Dodgers' lineup what it needs. Josue De Paula is an elite prospect who posted a 1.081 OPS in a late-season cup of coffee, yet Roberts can't bring himself to get him off the bennch.

Thank goodness the Dodgers can still pitch, to the tune of a 3.55 ERA in the regular season and now a 3.39 ERA in the postseason. Yet hidden in here, too, is another story of hubris.

Between Tanner Scott in 2025 and Edwin Díaz this year, throwing big money at a free-agent reliever in hopes of a quick fix for a persistently leaky bullpen has burned the Dodgers in consecutive seasons. And while their midseason trade for Skubal had plenty of merit on its own, it was a trade the Dodgers made not because they needed to, but because they could. Upgrade the offense or the bullpen? Nah, go get the best guy. It doesn't matter that he's another starter.

All of it has the Dodgers on the brink. They may be a $500 million team, but that number doesn't imply perfection so much as complacency. The Dodgers could afford to go bigger and better. They're about to have a legacy of leaving the job half-done.

To be clear, the Dodgers have a $340.6 million payroll and $165.9 million in luxury tax penalties attached to their 2026 roster . The latter alone is more than the $143.7 million the Brewers are spending on their roster.

According to MLB commissioner Rob Manfred, this matters. It matters so much that baseball must have a salary cap so teams like the Brewers can compete with teams like the Dodgers.

Yeah, one wonders how broken his brain is right now.

Even if the Brewers can't buy talent like the Dodgers, their nearly decade-long run of excellence is finally about to prove that identifying and maximizing talent can be just as effective, even despite being significantly cheaper. Jake Bauers , whose 3.3 rWAR for this season upped his seven-year career total to 2.0, knows what's up.

"There is a right way to play the game of baseball, and if you can commit to that and get an entire team to commit to that, you can overcome a lot of things," the veteran first baseman told ESPN's Jeff Passan . "As far as payrolls and all that, you've still got to play the game. And all the talent and all the money in the world can't buy the focus that you need to win baseball games."

Offensively, the average Brewer is almost four years younger than the average Dodger. Yet that's only an advantage in the abstract. What really matters is that the Brewers' offense:

Grinds at-bats, with the lowest swing rate in MLB

Puts runners on, with the highest OBP in MLB

Moves runners over, with the fifth-most stolen bases and sacrifice bunts in MLB

Hits in the clutch, with the second-highest AVG and SLG with runners in scoring position in MLB

The San Diego Padres felt this in the NLDS, especially when Jackson Chourio stung Mason Miller in Game 2. Now it's the Dodgers' turn in the NLCS. Milwaukee's offense brought out all its tricks i n Game 2, chasing Yamamoto after 2.2 innings and erasing not one, not two, but three deficits to win 7-4. Bauers had a hand in that with a 12-pitch walk. The sequel, an 11-pitch homer off Snell in Game 3, was even better.

On the other side, the Brewers play clean defense in support of nasty pitchers. Jacob Misiorowski can throw 105 mph, yet he's just one of 11 of 18 Brewers pitchers (min. 20 IP) who topped the league average of 94.7 mph on the fastball. It helps explain how they saw the Dodgers' 3.55 ERA and raised them a 3.51 ERA.

It also explains how the Dodgers' hitters' age has become a subplot in the NLCS. Brewers pitchers have been the storyline, particularly their bullpen. Milwaukee relievers have a 1.32 ERA for the series. Their average fastball? Try 98.5 mph.

Regardless of what happens next for the Brewers, GM Matt Arnold feels like a shoo-in for Executive of the Year. Pat Murphy should likewise have a third straight NL Manager of the Year in the bag. He has played the hand Arnold has dealt him masterfully, whether we're talking through new-school bullpen management or with an old-school chewing out of a rookie for violating the team's culture .

It's perhaps overly simple to distill this NLCS down to the best team money can buy versus the best team the mind can imagine. Yet that is more or less the truth. And whether the league likes it or not, the result in play has a refreshing message for the broader fanbase of Major League Baseball.

As much as it matters, there are some things money can't buy.

Stats courtesy of Baseball Reference , FanGraphs and Baseball Savant .

articles.title: Dodgers Down 0-3 in NLCS After Brewers Win, Box Score Stats, Highlights, Updated MLB Playoff Bracket
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers wrapped up a 6-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 3 of the NLCS at Dodger Stadium on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers wrapped up a 6-2 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 3 of the NLCS at Dodger Stadium on Wednesday night.

Milwaukee now owns a commanding 3-0 series lead, while Los Angeles is on the brink of elimination. The Dodgers haven't hit a home run in any of the first three games of the series.

Here's a look at key stats from the game:

And here's a look at the overall postseason bracket:

The Brewers didn't waste any time getting on the board, as Jackson Chourio hit a leadoff home run on the first pitch of the game.

The contest quickly turned into a pitching duel between Los Angeles' Blake Snell and Milwaukee's Robert Gasser, though. Neither team scored over the next four innings.

The Dodgers finally started to gain momentum in the bottom of the sixth, loading the bases with walks by Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Shohei Ohtani.

Los Angeles capitalized on the opportunity, jumping in front with a two-run double from Will Smith.

Still, a pair of strikeouts to finish the inning prevented the Dodgers from extending their lead.

The Brewers quickly responded in the top of the seventh, as Jake Bauers launched a two-run homer to cap off an 11-pitch at-bat.

Garrett Mitchell followed it up with a solo shot to give Milwaukee back-to-back home runs, pushing the team's advantage to 4-2.

Los Angeles' bullpen wasn't able to prevent the Brewers from tacking on another run in the top of the eighth, as Brice Turang scored on a wild pitch by Justin Wrobleski.

Milwaukee then gained a 6-2 lead with Joey Ortiz's RBI single in the ninth frame.

The Dodgers couldn't pull off a late rally, as Brewers closer Trevor Megill recorded four outs to clinch the victory.

Los Angeles finished with just five hits as a team, leaving eight runners on base and going 1-for-6 with runners in scoring position.

The Dodgers will attempt to keep their quest for a third consecutive World Series title alive in Game 4 on Thursday at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Brewers push Dodgers to brink, homer their way to 3-0 lead in NLCS
articles.summary: Only one team in MLB history has come back from down 3-0. The Dodgers' manager was on that team.
articles.body: The defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers are on the brink of elimination, with plenty of blame to go around.The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Dodgers 6-2 in Game 3 of the NLCS behind homers from Jackson Chourio, Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell on Wednesday. With that, the Brewers are one win away from their first World Series appearance since 1982. Only one team, the 2004 Boston Red Sox, has successfully come back from a 3-0 deficit in a best-of-seven series. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was famously part of that Red Sox team. Los Angeles can only hope that a similar miracle is in store.Game 4 is scheduled for 5 p.m. PT Thursday at Dodger Stadium, with Tyler Glasnow set to take the mound for the Dodgers against what will likely be either Dustin May or a bullpen game for Milwaukee.The Dodgers swept the Brewers in the NLCS last year. The Brewers are one win away from returning the favor. (AP Photo/Gregory Bull)AP Photo/Gregory BullBrewers got Blake Snell on the first pitch and the 11th pitchThis game ultimately came down to the beginning and ending of Dodgers starting pitcher Blake Snell's night. He allowed a home run on the very first pitch of the game, when Chourio ambushed a fastball in the middle of the zone for a solo homer.JACKSON CHOURIO GOES YARD ON THE FIRST PITCH OF GAME 3 🚀Brewers are looking to go up 3-0 in the series ‼️(via @MLB) pic.twitter.com/EsTde12e9D— Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) October 15, 2026 That homer loomed as the only run of the game for the first five innings, as Snell actually settled down and dominated. At one point, he retired 14 straight batters, and then the Dodgers' offense finally did something.L.A. didn't do it against Milwaukee starter Robert Gasser, who threw five scoreless innings and simply pounded the zone with sinkers against which the Dodgers couldn't do much. But with his pitch count at 72, Milwaukee pulled Gasser after five as he made his third trip through the Dodgers order.In came Brewers relief ace Abner Uribe, who hadn't allowed an earned run in his past 11 appearances between the regular season and postseason. It was the playbook the Brewers love, spamming their high-leverage arms to cover the back half of a game, but this time it worked out poorly.The Dodgers went walk, walk, strikeout, walk, double against Uribe, with Will Smith supplying that last hit after going 1-for-25 to begin the playoffs.Will Smith puts the Dodgers in front! pic.twitter.com/rrRQNDj3mL— MLB (@MLB) October 15, 2026 It was a huge momentum swing for the Dodgers, and it gave them their first lead of the game.It then swung right back on Snell's 99th pitch of the game — and his 101st.Similar to what he did against Dodgers Game 2 starter Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Bauers worked an 11-pitch at-bat against Snell that ended in a go-ahead, two-run homer following a leadoff walk from Andrew Vaughn.JAKE BAUERS AND GARRETT MITCHELL GO BACK-TO-BACK FOR MILWAUKEE 💪Brewers have a 4-2 lead in the seventh in Game 3 🔥(via @MLB) pic.twitter.com/7PGjzvcL30— Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) October 15, 2026 The Dodgers kept Snell in to face Mitchell. Two pitches later, the Brewers had another homer and reason to start scouting the teams in the ALCS in earnest. It was the first time in Snell's career that a pair of left-handed batters posted back-to-back homers against him. Together, Bauers and Mitchell posted more homers against Snell in this game than he allowed to lefties in the entire 2026 regular season.A list of all the left-handed batters to ever go yard off Blake Snell.Bauers/Mitchell first ever to go back-to-back. Only the second time that Snell has allowed two LHP homers in the same game.Absolutely stunning. pic.twitter.com/8dtri1Trr5— Jake Mintz (@Jake_Mintz) October 15, 2026 Milwaukee added more runs in the eighth and ninth innings, building their biggest lead of the postseason at four runs.NLCS has gone completely upside down for the DodgersThe odd part of this game was that it hardly looked like how the Brewers racked up 103 wins in the regular season, then motored through the NLDS against the San Diego Padres.Milwaukee was tied for 28th in MLB in homers during the regular season but is out-homering Los Angeles 5-0 in this series. Gasser is a traditional groundball pitcher, but only two of his 15 outs in Game 3 came on the ground, compared to 10 through the air and three via strikeout. The bullpen had to pick up Uribe, its most dominant arm of the past two years.Meanwhile, the Dodgers once again watched a member of their super-rotation leave the game with little reason to celebrate. They once again watched a lineup of veteran hitters fail to string hits together. They once again went homerless after ranking in the top 10 in MLB in homers this season.one subplot to monitor (among many) as the Dodgers try to avoid getting swept...since it was lengthened to best-of-7 in 1985, just 3 teams have hit 0 HR in the LCS1990 A's (swept BOS)1995 Reds (swept by ATL)2002 Twins (lost in 5 to LAA)...2026 Dodgers?! we'll see!— Céspedes Family BBQ (@CespedesBBQ) October 15, 2026 Los Angeles is now 3-for-29 with runners in scoring position this postseason. That's a.103 batting average. Those hits have come from only last season's trainwreck, Andy Pages, and Smith, who was shaping up to be this season's trainwreck. The team’s best postseason hitter overall has arguably been Kyle Tucker, the butt of every joke during the regular season.It feels almost academic whether or not Shohei Ohtani should keep playing on that bad knee — though he came out relatively well Wednesday, going 1-for-2 with a walk and hit-by-pitch. It doesn't matter if Ohtani is at his MVP-level best or barely able to walk; there's no title on the table with how the Dodgers have performed this postseason. They needed a similar RISP meltdown from the Atlanta Braves to get past the NLDS, and Milwaukee could not be less interested in doing L.A. a similar favor. Through three games, the Brewers have shown themselves to be the clearly better team — or at least, the only team with a functioning offense.A win Thursday would mean avenging last year's sweep at the hands of the Dodgers with their own sweep. A win at any point in the next four games would mean a trip to the Fall Classic. articles.title: Brewers stun Dodgers with back-to-back homers in 7th inning, take 3-0 lead in NLCS with 6-2 win
articles.summary: The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champion Dodgers to the brink of elimination.
articles.body: Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back homers off Blake Snell to regain the lead in the seventh inning, and the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday to take a 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series. Los Angeles had just taken a 2-1 lead in the sixth before getting stunned. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elimination. The only other time the Dodgers trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, they were swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the 1966 World Series. Game 4 is Thursday at Dodger Stadium, where the Brewers can become the first major-league club to complete a postseason sweep after getting swept by that same opponent in the previous postseason. Los Angeles took all four games against Milwaukee in the NLCS last year. The only team in big-league history to come back from a 3-0 deficit to win a postseason series was the Boston Red Sox in the 2004 AL Championship Series against the New York Yankees. Coming into the seventh, Snell had retired 14 batters in a row. The first pitch of the game thrown by the two-time Cy Young Award winner was hit for a home run by Jackson Chourio, and his last pitch was Mitchell’s solo shot. Andrew Vaughn drew a seven-pitch walk to open the inning and was replaced by pinch runner Christian Yelich. Bauers followed with a 412-foot shot to right field on the 11th pitch of the at-bat for a 3-2 lead as most of Milwaukee’s dugout came onto the field to celebrate. Mitchell was next and his drive traveled 428 feet to right-center, chasing Snell. It was the latest relentless plate appearance for Bauers, who drew a 12-pitch walk from Yoshinobu Yamamoto that helped the Brewers go ahead early in Game 3. Milwaukee, which has never beaten the Dodgers in three previous playoff series, is chasing its second pennant and first in the National League. The Brewers were in the American League when they reached their only World Series, a seven-game loss to the St. Louis Cardinals in 1982. Snell gave up four runs and four hits in six innings, struck out nine and walked two. The Brewers extended the lead to 5-2 in the eighth on Justin Wrobleski’s wild pitch that scored Brice Turang, who reached on an infield single and advanced to third on William Contreras’ single. They added another run on Joey Ortiz’s two-strike RBI single in the ninth. The offensively starved Dodgers took their first lead, 2-1, on Will Smith’s two-run double off reliever Abner Uribe in the sixth. Uribe followed rookie starter Robert Gasser, and he loaded the bases on walks to Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Shohei Ohtani. Smith, who was 1 for 25 in the playoffs, doubled off the left-center fence for his first hit of the NLCS. DL Hall took over from Uribe and stranded runners at second and third by striking out pinch hitter Kiké Hernández and Tommy Edman. Hall allowed one hit in 2 1/3 scoreless innings to improve to 3-0 in these playoffs. Trevor Megill got four outs for his second save of the series and fourth this postseason. The Dodgers played from behind again after the 22-year-old Chourio connected for his third career leadoff homer as fans were still heading to their seats. After that, Mitchell walked and Cooper Pratt singled in the second before Snell retired 14 in a row — six on strikeouts — before getting hammered in the seventh. The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings but couldn’t get enough across. They have yet to homer in the NLCS. Ohtani was 1 for 2 with a walk while hitting sixth in the order, the lowest he’s batted since joining the Dodgers three years ago.

articles.title: Brewers' bats stun Blake Snell, the Dodgers and their fans with emphatic victory to take 3-0 NLCS lead
articles.summary: The Dodgers are one loss away from their season and their run of dominance coming to an end.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — Blake Snell finally had a reason to look so tired.

Even when well-slept and in good spirits, the two-time Cy Young winner carries an exhausted, weary countenance on his 33-year-old face. Large bags make themselves at home beneath his eyes. When he pitches, they turn red and puffy. It's impossible to miss. As a result, Snell, a teetotaler, often appears worn out, stressed, overworked, even beleaguered as he's dicing opposing lineups to shreds.

But on Wednesday, in the seventh inning of NLCS Game 3 , Snell's shellshocked expression was shared by 50,708 others.

Jake Bauers, with whom Snell played in Tampa Bay's minor-league system, had just redirected a 97.8-mph heater into the right-field seats for a go-ahead, two-run homer. Adding to the drama: Bauers' series-altering, season-changing, dynasty-derailing long ball came on the 11th pitch of a hard-fought at-bat , Bauers' second such crucial plate appearance of this series. For six innings, Snell had looked utterly impenetrable. Brewers hitters had looked helpless. Bauers changed it all with a swing that will be remembered in Wisconsin for a long, long time.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season

As the baseball disappeared, Milwaukee's dugout — and the traveling Brewers fans behind it — exploded into revelry.

The rest of Dodger Stadium morphed, in an instant, into a library.

Things only grew more astonishing when the very next hitter, Garrett Mitchell, doubled up for a solo blast of his own. That left Snell and everyone else in disbelief. He was done, and so, it seems, were the Dodgers.

"Three home runs in a game?" A subdued Snell, who also gave up a big fly to Jackson Chourio on his very first pitch , said after Los Angeles' 6-2 defeat . "I mean, I didn't give up one all year. To give up three in a game, that's pretty frustrating."

Even more frustrating, for both Snell and the Dodgers, is that for about 15 minutes before Snell's implosion, this moribund juggernaut jolted itself and its fan base back to life. After being shut out and shut down for the first five innings by Milwaukee starter Robert Gasser, the Dodgers were gifted a window courtesy of ineffectively wild Brewers reliever Abner Uribe.

In the bottom of the sixth, Uribe offered free passes to three of the first four hitters he faced, loading the bases for scuffing Los Angeles catcher Will Smith, who entered Game 3 just 1-for-23 in October. But Uribe, intent on not walking home a run, piped a fastball to Smith, who clanged it off the midsection of the wall in deep left-center field. Two Dodgers scurried home. The yard erupted. Brewers skipper Pat Murphy inched toward the mound.

The series, it seemed, had flipped. Even when Milwaukee reliever DL Hall punched out the next two Dodgers, stranding two in scoring position, Chavez Ravine buzzed with a sense of optimism that this season, this magical run of dominance, was not dead yet.

That feeling, thanks in large part to Bauers, was remarkably short-lived.

"I was looking for a fastball, and I didn't want to miss it," the well-traveled first baseman explained in his postgame media conference. "I said I'll adjust to anything else, but get a heater — don't miss it."

That Bauers and Snell, former Rays farmhands who shared countless minor-league bus rides, ended up here, on this stage, is a testament to the long, winding, beautiful road that is professional baseball.

Wednesday's two main characters have taken very different paths in the decade since they last shared a clubhouse. Snell stuck with Tampa Bay, achieving stardom, two Cy Youngs and around $139 million in career earnings. Bauers, meanwhile, couldn't quite find a foothold in The Show. He bounced from organization to organization as filler, as depth, as a backup plan.

Twenty-six days before Snell penned his five-year, $182 million contract with the Dodgers in November 2024, Bauers was outrighted, effectively released, by the team he has since pushed within a game of the Fall Classic. But the Brewers, ahead of 2025, brought Bauers back on a minor-league deal. And through circumstance, faith, confidence, obstinance and determination, the 31-year-old SoCal kid finally turned himself into an impact major leaguer. This season, he was the best hitter on baseball's best team.

Over the past few days, he has taken things to a whole new level, looking as dialed in as a ballplayer can be.

"I've seen all the ups and downs he's been through, and it's been a lot of downs. So for him to go through this right now, he's earned it. Hats off to him," a conciliatory Snell shared after the game.

"This is the best I've ever seen him play."

The same sentiment cannot be said of Snell's Dodgers, who now find themselves at the bottom of a very steep mountain. Only one team in MLB history, the 2004 Red Sox, has ever crawled back from a 3-0 deficit in a best-of-seven series. That Dodgers manager Dave Roberts played on that legendary Boston team is more coincidence of history than useful rallying cry.

Make no bones about it; These Dodgers are in dire straits.

"We've got to give them something to cheer about," Roberts said about the understandably unenthused home fans in Game 3. "Kind of play downhill for a little bit, where I think it's just this whole series, they've outslugged us, outhit us."

By the ninth inning, even the overexuberant in-stadium hosts were struggling to keep up the spirits of the rapidly diminishing crowd.

"If you're still here, that means you're a true Dodger fan," one hollered.

In these parts, surrender is signaled not with white flags but with empty seats. There will likely be many of those here on Thursday, with the Dodgers playing for nothing but survival and a slim chance.

It's a stunning place for this sporting colossus to be, one loss away from a long winter of regret.

articles.title: Dave Roberts faces cruel MLB playoff twist as Dodgers fall into historic 3-0 hole against Brewers
articles.summary: The Dodgers are one loss from elimination, and their manager has a remarkable personal connection to the only successful comeback from a 3-0 deficit in MLB p...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers entered October attempting to accomplish something extraordinary. After winning consecutive World Series championships, they were pursuing a third straight title and another place in baseball history. Now they need a different kind of historical achievement simply to keep their season alive.

Milwaukee defeated Los Angeles 6-2 Wednesday night in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, taking a commanding 3-0 lead and moving within one victory of the World Series. The situation is particularly remarkable for Dodgers manager Dave Roberts.

Roberts was a member of the 2004 Boston Red Sox , the only team in MLB history to overcome a 3-0 deficit and win a best-of-seven postseason series.

Twenty-two years later, he must attempt to accomplish the same thing from the manager's seat.

A familiar situation with a very different perspective

The 2004 Red Sox were facing elimination against the New York Yankees when Roberts helped produce one of the most memorable moments in postseason history.

His stolen base in the ninth inning of Game 4 helped Boston tie the game and eventually begin its historic comeback. The Red Sox went on to win four consecutive games against New York before sweeping the St. Louis Cardinals in the World Series.

That comeback remains the only successful recovery from a 3-0 series deficit in MLB postseason history. Roberts now finds himself on the other side of that seemingly impossible equation.

According to MLB's historical records, teams holding a 3-0 lead in a best-of-seven postseason series have won 41 of 42 completed series.

The only exception was Roberts' Red Sox. Those numbers demonstrate how difficult the Dodgers' challenge has become.

Blake Snell's seventh inning changed everything

For six innings Wednesday, Los Angeles appeared capable of beginning its comeback. Blake Snell had recovered from allowing Jackson Chourio's leadoff home run and was dominating Milwaukee's lineup.

The Dodgers took a 2-1 lead in the sixth inning when Will Smith delivered a two-run double, giving the home crowd its first major reason for optimism.

Snell walked Andrew Vaughn to open the seventh inning before Jake Bauers worked an extraordinary 11-pitch at-bat. Bauers eventually connected for a two-run home run, putting Milwaukee back in front.

Garrett Mitchell followed with another homer, ending Snell's evening and giving the Brewers a lead they would never relinquish.

Los Angeles managed only five hits in the defeat. For a lineup featuring Shohei Ohtani , Mookie Betts, Kyle Tucker and other established offensive stars, the inability to consistently produce runs has become the defining issue of the series.

Los Angeles will turn to Tyler Glasnow in Game 4 on Thursday night. The right-hander faces the responsibility of keeping the Dodgers' championship hopes alive against a Milwaukee team that has repeatedly responded whenever Los Angeles threatens to take control.

The Dodgers have overcome postseason adversity before, including elimination threats during their previous championship runs. But winning four consecutive games against a team that has controlled the first three meetings represents a substantially different challenge.

Roberts knows better than almost anyone that the impossible can occasionally happen in October. He also knows how rare those moments are.

The Dodgers have spent the last two seasons making history by winning championships. Now their manager needs to recreate a piece of baseball history that he helped write more than two decades ago.

articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers, Robert Gasser, make MLB postseason history in thrilling Game 3 victory
articles.summary: Prior to the start of the 2026 MLB regular season, just about every national baseball analyst predicted that the Milwaukee Brewers would regress dramatically...
articles.body:
Prior to the start of the 2026 MLB regular season, just about every national baseball analyst predicted that the Milwaukee Brewers would regress dramatically. Not only did most think that they would finish third or worse in the National League Central Division, but many set their win total in the low-to-mid 80s.

Now, the Brewers are one win away from the World Series.

After finishing the regular season 103-59, the best record in baseball, Milwaukee has taken the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers to the brink. With their thrilling victory on Wednesday night, the Brewers now have a 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series. One more win will give them just their second ever World Series appearance.

Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Robert Gasser and hitters Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell made history

After winning the first two games in Milwaukee, the Brewers turned to rookie left-hander Robert Gasser to start Game Three. He had previously been the starting pitcher in Game Four of the NLDS when Milwaukee defeated the San Diego Padres on the road in order to get to this point in the first place.

The rookie delivered. While Dodgers starter Blake Snell cruised after giving up a leadoff home run to Jackson Chourio, Gasser matched him by putting up zero after zero after zero.

All told, Gasser pitched five strong innings, allowing just three hits and a walk while striking out three. He did not allow any runs.

Milwaukee's southpaw is the first rookie pitcher in MLB history with a scoreless postseason start against the defending World Series champions.

After Gasser was removed from the game, reliever Abner Uribe gave up the lead by allowing two runs to score. Thankfully, DL Hall bailed him out by limiting the damage. However, the Brewers trailed 2-1.

In the top of the seventh, first baseman Jake Bauers battled Snell with an 11-pitch at-bat. He ended the standoff by launching a two-run home run into right-centerfield. Garrett Mitchell followed with a solo home run, giving Milwaukee a 4-2 advantage.

These back-to-back bombs also made MLB history:

Never, in the history of regular or postseason baseball, had a team hit back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning or later on the road off a multiple-time Cy Young Award winner that turned a deficit into a lead.

It truly was a special team performance, and it was just another reminder to fans how special this Brewers team is. Now, Milwaukee will look to Game Four on Thursday night and try to do something just one team in franchise history has done before: advance to the World Series.

articles.title: Dodgers' Dave Roberts Says He Won't Use 2004 Red Sox as Inspiration for Team Amid NLCS Deficit
articles.summary: Facing a 3-0 series hole after blowing a late lead in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, Dave Roberts won't return to the most famous moment from his playing career in an effort to help inspire a Los Angeles Dodgers turnaround.
articles.body:
Facing a 3-0 series hole after blowing a late lead in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, Dave Roberts won't return to the most famous moment from his playing career in an effort to help inspire a Los Angeles Dodgers turnaround.

Speaking to reporters after Wednesday's 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers, Roberts explained he doesn't plan to bring up the 2004 Boston Red Sox when he addresses the Dodgers before Game 4.

"I think they've seen the documentary," Roberts said. "They know it can happen."

Brewers have Dodgers' dynasty on life support

Roberts lives in MLB history forever because his stolen base in the bottom of the ninth in Game 4 of the ALCS between the Red Sox and New York Yankees helped them keep the series alive.

The 2004 Red Sox remain the only MLB team that has overcome a 3-0 series deficit. They rattled off eight consecutive wins between the ALCS and World Series to end the franchise's 86-year championship drought.

There are some similarities to be gleaned from that Red Sox team and this year's Dodgers. Both of them had key players dealing with injuries that left their status unclear at one point.

Curt Schilling had an ankle procedure during the series after suffering an injury late in the regular season. He famously pitched Game 6 in the Bronx with blood visible on the sock on his right leg.

Shohei Ohtani was reportedly uncertain to play in Game 3 against the Brewers due to his ongoing physical issues, though Roberts wound up keeping him in the lineup. He hit sixth in the order, his lowest position in a game he started since Sept. 19, 2020.

One thing the Dodgers can do to convince themselves a comeback is possible is look at the pitching matchups if they can get past Game 4. Tyler Glasnow is scheduled to start on Thursday.

If the Dodgers win that game, Tarik Skubal would come back on regular rest in Game 5 on Friday. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, coming off the worst start of his playoff career in Game 2, would pitch in a potential Game 6 on Sunday.

Game 7 would be all hands on deck for both teams. Kevin Millar famously said "don't let us win tonight" in reference to Game 4 for the Red Sox because they had Pedro Martinez in Game 5 and Schilling in Game 6.

The Dodgers are down 3-0 in a best-of-seven series for the first time since the 1966 World Series against the Baltimore Orioles. That didn't well for Los Angeles because the Orioles closed it out in Game 4.

Nothing the Dodgers have done in this series thus far indicates a comeback will happen, but Roberts knows better than almost anyone that it is possible.

articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call has criticized Major League Baseball over a Sydney Sweeney sports betting commercial airing during the
articles.body: Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Alex Call has criticized Major League Baseball over a Sydney Sweeney sports betting commercial airing during the postseason, arguing that its content is not suitable for family viewing. Call raised the issue on social media on October 14, saying he struggles to explain the advertisement to his young son when they watch baseball together. His complaint puts the spotlight on a question MLB and its broadcast partners face during playoff games: how should they balance commercial deals with the expectations of families watching one of America's most popular sports? Call's objection was direct, and he made his reason personal.Alex Call calls out MLB over Sydney Sweeney’s playoff adCall quote-tweeted a post criticizing commercials shown during the MLB postseason and took particular issue with an ad featuring Sweeney. The actress appears nude but is covered by sports balls in the sports betting campaign. For Call, the problem was not simply the advertisement's suggestive presentation. It was the possibility of it appearing unexpectedly during a game watched by children.“Can we please get the soft porn ads off playoff broadcasts, TBS, Fox, NBC, @MLB? My son wants to watch baseball with Dada, but how do I justify that when a half-naked women could come on screen anytime?? This is America’s Pastime. Parents shouldn’t have to worry about this,” Call wrote.The wording made his concern clear. Call wants baseball broadcasts to remain suitable for parents who watch games with their children, without having to anticipate what might appear during a commercial break.His criticism also places MLB's role in the conversation. Playoff games reach large audiences across several networks, and advertisements form a key part of the broadcast business. But viewers do not always agree on what belongs in that setting, particularly when a campaign relies on sexual imagery to attract attention.Call was not on the Dodgers' postseason roster, according to Men's Journal. His comments therefore came from outside the team's active playoff lineup, even as Los Angeles faced pressure on the field.Sweeney releases another version of the commercialSweeney has since posted a new version of the campaign on social media. In the latest ad, she appears wearing only white Novig underwear while addressing the attention surrounding betting markets tied to her clothing.“There are grown men making spreadsheets to bet on what color underwear I’m wearing,” Sweeney says in the commercial. “I mean, I’m flattered?”The new version gives the campaign another talking point, but Call's complaint focuses on where such advertising appears rather than on Sweeney personally. His post questions whether viewers should encounter this material during mainstream baseball broadcasts, where parents may expect to watch games with their children without worrying about suggestive content.Sweeney has not publicly responded to Call's criticism, according to Men's Journal. The exchange also leaves an important distinction: an advertisement designed to provoke attention may work as a marketing campaign, but that does not mean every viewer will welcome it during a live sporting event.For MLB, the debate reaches beyond one commercial. Networks carry postseason games to broad audiences, and advertisers want campaigns that stand out. Call's objection highlights the tension between those commercial interests and the family-friendly image baseball has long promoted. articles.title: Max Muncy gives blunt assessment of Dodgers' performance vs. Brewers in NLCS: 'We're playing like s***'
articles.summary: Max Muncy had a simple explanation for the Dodgers' 3-0 deficit in the NLCS.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are suddenly in big trouble. After yet another loss Wednesday, the Dodgers find themselves down 3-0 in the National League Championship Series. With another loss, they'll be eliminated from the postseason.

This wasn't the way it was supposed to be. In year's past, the Dodgers' depth and financial muscle won out against the best teams in the game. Something is different this time around and Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy thinks he knows exactly what's going on.

When asked, Muncy summed things up succinctly saying, "We're playing like s***."

Muncy, of course, made sure to give the Milwaukee Brewers credit. After lamenting his own team's struggles, Muncy added, "[The Brewers] are playing great. It's as simple as that."

Much has been made of the struggles of Dodgers two-way star Shohei Ohtani this postseason, but he wasn't the problem Wednesday. After being dropped to sixth in the batting order, Ohtani reached base three times in the contest.

His overall numbers, however, are still a problem, as Ohtani is hitting just .182 in the series. Many of his teammates have similar batting averages, including Freddie Freeman, Teoscar Hernandez and Muncy, none of whom is hitting above .192. Catcher Will Smith is hitting under .100.

While those struggles can be written off as small-sample outcomes … the NLCS is a small sample. All it takes is a few bad games from your star players to decide the outcome of a series. The Dodgers are experiencing that phenomenon right now.

Because of that, though, it won't take much for the Dodgers to claw their way back into the series. While 3-0 comebacks are highly unlikely, they are not impossible . All it would take is the Dodgers' stars hitting like they should.

Even then, that might not be enough. In order to stage a comeback, the Dodgers also need the Brewers to give them an opening, which seems unlikely given how well Milwaukee is playing right now.

articles.title: New MLB Rumors on Phillies' Talks With Chase Utley, Raul Ibanez Before Don Mattingly Decision
articles.summary: Don Mattingly, who was officially named manager of the Philadelphia Phillies on Wednesday, might have been the fourth choice for the job.
articles.body:
Don Mattingly, who was officially named manager of the Philadelphia Phillies on Wednesday, might have been the fourth choice for the job.

Per The Athletic's Jayson Stark , the Phillies reached out to former players Chase Utley and Raul Ibañez to "gauge their interest" in the managerial job.

Stark noted both Utley and Ibañez "politely declined" the opportunity.

In addition to Utley and Ibañez, Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski previously spoke with Alex Cora about the job. Cora declined because he intends to sit out the 2027 MLB season.

Utley played 13 of his 16 MLB seasons with the Phillies. He ranks in the top 10 in franchise history in games played, hits, total bases and home runs. He was also a key member of the 2008 team that won the World Series.

Ibañez spent three seasons with the Phillies from 2009 to '11. His lone All-Star appearance during his 19-year career came during his first year in Philadelphia when he hit a career-high 34 homers.

Both Utley and Ibañez currently work in the front office for the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Ibañez has been with the Dodgers since January 2024 when he was hired as vice president of baseball development and special projects. Utley works as a special assistant to president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman.

The Phillies previously expressed interest in hiring Utley in some capacity before he joined the Dodgers, but the six-time All-Star told Conor Smith of the Philadelphia Inquirer earlier this year that being close to his home in Los Angeles was the main selling point.

"I finished my career in Los Angeles," Utley said. "I live in Los Angeles, and I wanted to still be around baseball, but still be around my family and not travel too much."

According to Stark, the Phillies' interest in Utley and Ibañez was "serious enough" that Dombrowski requested formal permission from the Dodgers to speak with both men.

Utley told Stark that managing an MLB club was "not realistic" for him at this point.

Mattingly was named interim manager by Philadelphia on April 28 after Rob Thomson was fired following a 9-19 start to the season.

The Phillies responded to the managerial change by going 79-55 under Mattingly. Only the Milwaukee Brewers, Tampa Bay Rays and Los Angeles Dodgers had better records during that period.

Philadelphia made the playoffs as a wild card, losing in the NL Wild Card series in three games to the Atlanta Braves. It marked the third straight season the Phillies have lost their first playoff series.

Mattingly, who signed a two-year deal with the Phillies, had not managed since the 2022 season with the Miami Marlins. He has a 968-1,005 career record in 13 seasons as a manager.

articles.title: World Series 2026 Predictions, Full Schedule and Bracket Picks for Fall Classic
articles.summary: Major League Baseball hasn't seen a World Series three-peat since the New York Yankees went back-to-back-to-back from 1998 to 2000.
articles.body:
Major League Baseball hasn't seen a World Series three-peat since the New York Yankees went back-to-back-to-back from 1998 to 2000.

Barring a miracle, it looks like that drought will continue.

The Los Angeles Dodgers, champions of the past two seasons, are sitting on the brink of elimination following their 6-2 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday. Milwaukee now has an overwhelming 3-0 lead in the series and will host the next two games (if the second is even necessary).

As far as the NLCS goes, things seem all but cemented. Still, there's another league championship playing out and a World Series to follow, so there's plenty left to be figured out. And, hey, if anyone can crawl out of a hole this deep, you would think it would be a team with L.A.'s blend of talent and big-stage experience, so maybe a surprise could still happen.

Game 1: ALCS winner at NLCS winner on Fox

Game 2: ALCS winner at NLCS winner on Fox

Game 3: NLCS winner at ALCS winner on Fox

Game 4: NLCS winner at ALCS winner on Fox

Game 5: NLCS winner at ALCS winner on Fox*

Game 6: ALCS winner at NLCS winner on Fox*

Before crowning a predicted World Series winner, a predicted matchup must be set.

Again, on the NL side, that seems easy. The Dodgers aren't mathematically out of it, but history says they face a near impossible task. If they somehow completed a comeback from down 3-0, they'd double the list of teams to have ever pulled it off.

The ALCS, meanwhile, feels more like a coin flip, as it'll be a best-of-five from here. The Rays have been the better team this season, but the Guardians are in a groove (4-1 over their last five) and have wrestled away home-field advantage. It still feels like Tampa will get this figured out.

If this winds up with a Brewers-Rays finale, that series could have all-time potential pitting the top seeds from each league against one another. Plus, they share a ton of similarities, both with their situations as small-market clubs and with their on-field approaches.

Tampa is an awesome team, and it can win contests in myriad ways, but who's picking against Milwaukee right now? Certainly not us. The Brewers had the best regular season (by wins and run differential), and they might be on the verge of sweeping the two-time defending champs.

Prediction: Brewers over Rays in six games.

articles.title: Phillies Hire Former Mets Manager Carlos Mendoza to Don Mattingly's Coaching Staff After Firings
articles.summary: Having formally announced the hiring of Don Mattingly as their full-time manager on Wednesday, Philadelphia Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski has made another addition to the coaching staff.
articles.body:
Having formally announced the hiring of Don Mattingly as their full-time manager on Wednesday, Philadelphia Phillies president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski has made another addition to the coaching staff.

Dombrowski announced on Thursday that former New York Mets manager Carlos Mendoza will be the infield and third base coach on Mattingly's staff.

Another key takeaway from Dombrowski's press conference was Trea Turner's future at shortstop. He said the plan is to have Turner open 2027 at his usual spot, but he will need to prove throughout the year that he can stay there.

Brewers have Dodgers' dynasty on life support

Infield defense was a huge problem for the Phillies this season, with Turner's decline being a primary culprit. He graded out as one of the best defensive shortstops in MLB in 2025, but his minus-eight outs above average this year was tied for 16th out of 19 qualified for shortstops.

It didn't help matters that Turner had the worst offensive season of his career with a .242/.297/.378 slash line in 157 games. He is owed $27.3 million every year through the 2033 season on his current contract.

Mendoza spent three seasons with the Mets from 2024 to '26. He was fired midway through this season after a 34-47 start, but his overall record was a solid 206-199.

The Mets made the playoffs in Mendoza's first year when they advanced to the NLCS before losing to the Los Angeles Dodgers in six games.

Anthony Contreras, who was promoted to third-base coach during the 2026 season, is expected to remain with the club in a different role, per The Athletic's Matt Gelb .

Philadelphia's managerial job came open on April 28 when Rob Thomson was fired amid a 9-19 start to the 2026 season. He ended his tenure with 355 career wins, 10th-most in franchise history.

It looked like this was the start of a dramatic fall for the Phillies after making the playoffs in each of the previous four years, but they rebounded under Mattingly with a 79-55 record to clinch a playoff berth.

The Phillies are in a tricky position going forward that Mattingly will have to help them navigate. They entered 2026 with the third-oldest collection of position players by average age.

That's not a problem when Bryce Harper and Kyle Schwarber are still raking, but other members of that group do seem like they have hit the wrong side of the aging curve. Turner, J.T. Realmuto and Alec Bohm are below-average hitters by OPS+.

The rotation is also likely to be entering a transition phase sooner than later. Aaron Nola had another difficult year after a rough 2025. Zack Wheeler remains dominant, but he will turn 37 in May and is entering the final year of his current deal.

Philadelphia's farm system has players with high-impact potential at the very top, but the group thins out quickly afterward. Andrew Painter's improvement after the All-Star break is an encouraging sign going forward.

Aidan Miller was limited to just four games in the minors in 2026 due to a back injury. He raked in the minors during the 2025 campaign with a .264/.392/.433 slash line in 116 games across two levels. Justin Crawford earned a spot on the 26-man roster out of spring training, but struggled in his first test against MLB pitching.

It seems likely that this could turn into a rebuilding situation sooner than later, but the bottom hasn't dropped off yet based on how this group rebounded after a slow start that led to Thomson's firing.

It's a dramatic turnaround for Mattingly, who was prepared to retire before his son and Phillies general manager, Preston Mattingly, talked him into coaching on Thomson's staff in 2026.

The ripple effects of that move are astounding looking at it now, though no one was anticipating Thomson to be dismissed 28 games into the season.

There is a risk of promoting the interim manager after a brief period of success, but Mattingly also has extensive managerial experience in big markets that he won't be overwhelmed by this.

Mattingly had 12 years of experience as a manager from 2011 to '22. He spent five seasons with the Los Angeles Dodgers, then moved on to the Miami Marlins prior to the 2016 season.

The 65-year-old won NL Manager of the Year in 2020 after leading the Marlins to the playoffs. He owns a 968-1,005 career managerial record including his interim record with the Phillies from 2026.

articles.title: MLB playoff team payroll: One surprising fact shows how much more the Dodgers spend compared to Brewers, Rays, Guardians
articles.summary: The Dodgers' spending habits are out of control compared to the three other playoff teams.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are on the brink of playoff elimination . Following another loss to the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday, Los Angeles now trails 3-0 in the National League Championship Series. With another loss, the team with far and away the highest payroll remaining would be eliminated.

But to simply call the Dodgers a high-payroll team in this instance doesn't capture the full picture. Among the four remaining playoff teams, the Dodgers haven't just outspent the competition; they've demolished it.

Just how large is the payroll disparity between the four teams left in the MLB playoffs? Well, the Dodgers actually have a higher payroll than the three other teams combined.

Coming into the playoffs, the Dodgers carried a $338 million payroll, per USA Today via the MLB Labor Relations Department. That figure was the second-highest in MLB, with only the New York Mets spending more in 2026, given the Dodgers' salary deferrals.

By comparison, the Milwaukee Brewers rank 19th with a $143.5 million payroll, the Tampa Bay Rays rank 25th with a $98.3 million payroll and the Cleveland Guardians rank 30th with a $74.2 million payroll. Add those figures together, and you get $316 million. You could still add Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $16 million salary to that figure and come in under $338 million.

To further highlight the payroll disparity between the four remaining teams, here are a few fun facts about each team's spending habits:

(All contract data via Cots Baseball Contracts)

Players who made over $20 million in 2026

Dodgers: Six. Kyle Tucker, Tyler Glasnow, Shohei Ohtani, Blake Snell, Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman.

Brewers: Two. Christian Yelich and Brandon Woodruff.

Most expensive offseason addition for 2026

Dodgers: Kyle Tucker on a four-year, $240 million contract

Brewers: Brandon Woodruff on a $22 million qualifying offer

Guardians: Sean Armstrong on a one-year, $5.5 million deal

Rays: Steven Matz on a two-year, $15 million deal

Dodgers: Shohei Ohtani's 10-year, $700 million deal

Brewers: Christian Yelich's nine-year, $215 million extension

Guardians: Jose Ramirez's seven-year, $175 million extension

Rays: Wander Franco's 11-year, $182 million extension

Well, in addition to presenting a fun David vs. Goliath storyline during the playoffs, MLB has made it a significant issue. With a lockout on the horizon, the league and its owners have already put out a coordinated campaign pushing for a salary cap as part of the next collective-bargaining agreement.

The Dodgers and their payroll are at the center of that campaign. Yes, the league put out an entire campaign aimed at tearing down one of its most popular and successful teams.

A Dodgers loss wouldn't stop MLB from continuing to push that storyline, but it would poke a hole in the league's reasoning. As the Brewers, Guardians and Rays have shown this postseason, money can be an advantage, but it's not the only way to win.

articles.title: MLB Insider Reveals Derek Jeter's Past Talks With Jazz Chisholm Jr., 'Get Your Head on Right'
articles.summary: The last gasp of Jazz Chisholm's tenure with the New York Yankees may have been being used as a pinch hitter in Game 3 of the ALDS after manager Aaron Boone benched him to start the game due to his struggles at the plate and in the field.
articles.body:
The last gasp of Jazz Chisholm's tenure with the New York Yankees may have been being used as a pinch hitter in Game 3 of the ALDS after manager Aaron Boone benched him to start the game due to his struggles at the plate and in the field.

Per Bob Klapisch of the Newark Star Ledger , Chisholm's erratic performance on the field has been an issue dating back to his time with the Miami Marlins when then-minority owner and Yankees legend Derek Jeter met with him to tell "him to get his head straight" as part of a series of conversations:

"When Jazz was in Miami, Derek Jeter was there as the owner and Don Mattingly was the manager. That's two great Yankees who understood tradition and played the game right. They both met with Chisholm on repeated occasions and begged him to get his head straight. 'You have superstar talent. You have to get your head right. You have to focus. You have to make this a priority.' Not even they could get through. The Yankees knew all this when they traded for Jazz. It's not like Chisholm's reputation was a mystery to them. But they thought that a clubhouse filled with veterans like Aaron Judge and Cody Bellinger and Gerrit Cole could get through to him."

After going 0-for-6 at the plate in the first two games against the Tampa Bay Rays and committing a costly error in Game 2, Chisholm was benched for Anthony Volpe to start Game 3.

Chisholm, who is set to become a free agent this offseason, told reporters after the Yankees' 4-3 loss that ended their season he wasn't given any advance word about not being in the starting lineup.

"I'd always prefer a conversation, so I would at least know what I'm walking into," Chisholm said.

That came after Chisholm also didn't play Game 1 of the AL Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox, though Yankees manager Aaron Boone made him aware ahead of time that was going to be the case.

Chisholm was originally signed by the Arizona Diamondbacks as an international free agent in 2015. He was traded to Miami in July 2019, then made his big-league debut the following year.

Jeter purchased an ownership stake in the Marlins in 2017 and held the title of CEO for the organization. He remained in that position until February 2022 when he stepped down reportedly in part due to differences with majority owner Bruce Sherman over payroll spending.

Chisholm had plenty of ups and downs throughout his time in Miami, but the highs suggested a player with superstar potential. He hit 14 homers in 60 games during an injury-plagued 2022 season, earning his first All-Star appearance.

That performance helped Chisholm earn the cover spot on MLB The Show 23 . He is the only Marlins player to grace the cover of the popular video game.

After more injuries limited him to 97 games in 2023 and a slow start the following year, the Marlins traded Chisholm to New York midway through the 2024 campaign.

Last year was the best of Chisholm's career with a .242/.332/.481 slash line, 31 homers and 31 stolen bases. He came into the season targeting a 50-50 year, but he slumped down to 19 homers in 137 games. He did steal a career-high 41 bases.

Chisholm's defensive metrics have been all over the place throughout his career. This season was a down year, as he finished 15th out of 17 qualified second basemen in defensive runs saved. He did grade out well in outs above average and field run value.

All of this is to show how difficult an evaluation Chisholm will be as a free agent. He will be among the youngest players in this class with his 29th birthday not until Feb. 1, so a team could easily bet on his upside to be a difference-maker.

articles.title: Tigers breakout star cleared medically for ‘normal offseason’
articles.summary: Tigers receive encouraging injury news about young pitcher.
articles.body:
The Detroit Tigers have received encouraging MLB injury news, as starting pitcher Troy Melton has been medically cleared and is expected to enjoy a normal offseason after ending the 2026 campaign with forearm issues.

Tigers released some good news regarding Troy Melton. He's been cleared medically, no damage to his arm, and will have a normal offseason — Chris McCosky (@cmccosky) October 15, 2026

Tigers released some good news regarding Troy Melton. He's been cleared medically, no damage to his arm, and will have a normal offseason

Chris McCosky (@cmccosky) October 15, 2026

The Tigers announced Thursday that the sophomore right-hander has no damage to his arm, providing a significant boost for an organization counting on him to remain a key part of its starting rotation moving forward.

Melton's season ended prematurely in September after he experienced right forearm tightness and fatigue. With concerns surrounding his health, Detroit will be relieved to learn that the young pitcher can begin preparing for next season without an extended recovery period.

Sep 14, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Detroit Tigers starting pitcher Troy Melton (52) pitches to the Toronto Blue Jays during the first inning at Rogers Centre. Mandatory Credit: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images

Melton's 2026 campaign came to an abrupt end on Sept. 20, when he left a start against the Chicago White Sox after just 3.2 innings. He was subsequently placed on the injured list, ending a promising season for one of Detroit's most important young arms.

The injury concerns were not entirely new. Melton also dealt with elbow inflammation during spring training, which delayed his season debut until May 24.

Given those previous issues, Thursday's medical update represents an important development for both Melton and the Tigers. Being cleared with no arm damage should allow the right-hander to focus on his offseason preparation rather than rehabilitation.

Although the team will undoubtedly monitor his workload and health moving forward, the expectation of a normal offseason offers optimism heading into 2027.

Tigers counting on young pitcher after strong season

Jul 17, 2026; Anaheim, California, USA; Detroit Tigers pitcher Troy Melton (52) is greeted by teammates after a pitching change during the sixth inning against the Los Angeles Angels at Angel Stadium. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images

Despite the injury setbacks, Melton established himself as a valuable member of Detroit's rotation in 2026. He made 20 regular-season starts, finishing with an 8-5 record, a 2.76 ERA and a 1.13 WHIP.

The right-hander also recorded 94 strikeouts while allowing 35 earned runs on 92 hits, demonstrating his ability to compete effectively against major-league hitters.

Those numbers make Melton an important piece of the Tigers' pitching plans, particularly as the organization looks to improve after a disappointing season.

Detroit finished the year with a 76-86 record, placing fourth in the American League Central and missing the MLB postseason for the first time since 2023.

With the Tigers looking to rebound next season, Melton's health could play a significant role in their chances of returning to contention.

Thursday's announcement provides a welcome reason for optimism. If Melton carries his 2026 form into next season while staying healthy, he could remain one of Detroit's most valuable young pitchers.

articles.title: Brewers Rookie Made MLB History In Game 3 Win Over Dodgers
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are one win away from their first National League pennant since 1982
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are one win away from sweeping the Los Angeles Dodgers, and have gotten to this point without Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson having their best starts.

Henderson made two costly errors in Game 2 of the series, and Misiorowski went just 4 1/3 innings in Game 1, allowing five hits and walking three batters. However, in Game 3, Robert Gasser stepped up big time. He went five innings, matching Henderson for the longest start by a Brewer this postseason. However, unlike Henderson's five-inning start against the San Diego Padres, Gasser did not allow a run.

According to OptaSTATS , Gasser is the first rookie in MLB history to record a scoreless start in the postseason against the defending champions.

Gasser came to Milwaukee in the Josh Hader trade in 2022. He made his debut in 2024, but before this season, he had only played in seven regular-season games. He underwent Tommy John surgery after his first five career starts and did not return until late in 2025. His rookie status was intact through this season.

There were serious questions about who would be pitching for the Brewers after Misiorowski and Henderson. Well, Gasser has stepped up big time, and it's not crazy to say he has actually been their best starter this postseason. If the Brewers win it all, Gasser will be remembered for gutsy road performances against the Padres and Dodgers.

The job for the Brewers is not finished, and unless the Dodgers come back from a 3-0 deficit, Gasser will draw a start in the Fall Classic as well.

Alex Call is taking issue with suggestive ads that air during MLB games

The Dodgers outfielder shared his outrage on X in a post

Alex Call is calling foul on recent commercials that he says feature "half-naked women."

In the commercials, the Euphoria actress, 29, bares almost all while posing in provocative positions.

"Just you, your takes and sports," Sweeney, topless and holding her breasts, says into the camera.

Call — who was left off the Dodgers' postseason roster — has had time to watch games at home with his family amid the team's playoff run.

The right fielder also made headlines earlier this season for his position — in which he nearly injured Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani .

In July, Call clipped Ohtani's right elbow with his cleat while jumping over the dugout railing to celebrate the team's win against the Philadelphia Phillies.

articles.title: Phillies reunion with polarizing infielder 'can't be ruled out' per MLB insider
articles.summary: While it'd be a mild surprise, this reunion is not out of the question just yet.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies lost in the postseason once again, and now the fan base is hoping to see some big changes after the team has continued to run it back for a few years now.

While Don Mattingly is back, the Phillies have already moved on from Bobby Dickerson and Kevin Long and have hired Carlos Mendoza to fill a coaching role. But when it comes to player personnel, there's one player many fans are likely hoping departs.

This polarizing infielder, Alec Bohm, is set to be a free agent this offseason. However, MLB insider Robert Murray of Fansided.com believes that it's not out of the question that Bohm will actually return to the Phillies this offseason.

MLB insider won't rule out Phillies re-signing Alec Bohm this offseason

"A return to Philadelphia can't be ruled out, but with so many teams looking for right-handed hitters, Bohm should have plenty of suitors in free agency," Murray writes. "And it would surprise no one if his best days were still ahead of him."

Bohm is one of the most polarizing players from the last few seasons of Phillies baseball. He's had his fair share of great moments, but also plenty of lowlights.

Across seven seasons and 874 total games with the Phillies since 2020, he's posted just 4.9 bWAR, with his -0.2 bWAR mark this past season being the second-worst of his MLB career.

He's not much of a home-run hitter, with only 85 since his MLB debut. He does knock in a lot of baserunners, with 483 RBIs in his MLB career. But with a .273 batting average and a .735 OPS, Bohm isn't much more than an average hitter.

The Phillies potentially re-signing him would not likely sit well with some fans, especially since he'd be another example of this Phillies franchise running it back in recent years.

A new face in the infield would be nice for this Phillies team. It could be top prospect Aidan Miller, or another free agent or trade option to fill in for Bohm.

While Murray isn't ruling out Bohm returning to the Phillies, with his note that Bohm's market might be strong, it's hard to imagine the Phillies doubling down on Bohm after a frustrating 2026 season for the 30-year-old infielder.

articles.title: Christian Yelich issues urgent reminder despite Brewers’ 3-0 NLCS lead over Dodgers
articles.summary: Christian Yelich knows the job isn’t done. The Milwaukee Brewers are in a favorable position with their 3-0 National League Championship Series lead over the...
articles.body:
Christian Yelich knows the job isn't done. The Milwaukee Brewers are in a favorable position with their 3-0 National League Championship Series lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers, but the fact of the matter is that it is a best-of-seven series. Milwaukee has to win one more game to clinch its first World Series appearance since 1982 — and the two-time defending champion Dodgers won't go away quietly .
